correctness.rationale: Qin Theorem 1.1 supplies a unique strictly positive equilibrium and almost-sure edge growth for every prescribed positive firing-rate vector. Divide the equilibrium by m_e^alpha to obtain s=B r. For two rate vectors with the same m, the difference of r is exactly in ker B; conversely any positive r with Br=s defines rates whose same m is the unique equilibrium. Connectedness gives ker B=0 on nonbipartite graphs and span(bipartition signs) on bipartite graphs; strict positivity yields the exact interval. On cycles direct differentiation at m_i=q_i=p yields L=(1-alpha/2)I+(alpha/4)(shift+shift^{-1}), with eigenvalues 1-alpha sin^2(pi k/n)>=1-alpha>0; the analytic implicit-function theorem and Fourier diagonalization give the exact derivative and norm. Optimizing c/(1-alpha(1-c^2)) proves the discrete first crossover and continuum envelope. Standalone CHECK.py passed 1460 deterministic corroborations including heterogeneous non-cycle graph fibers. The universal results are proved analytically, not by enumeration.

originality.rationale: The principal published source proves existence and uniqueness of the positive equilibrium, and explicitly presents the transformed flux equation on which our proof depends. It does not state the complete inverse firing-rate equivalence classes, finite-graph bipartiteness identifiability criterion, or sharp nonuniform-rate cycle susceptibility/crossover found here. Prior WARM cycle spectral stability in a strong-reinforcement regime is credited and compared by implication, not title alone. The 2012 related graph-based urn has different state and allocation geometry. Multiple actual published-literature and published-finding corpus semantic searches, plus prior research records claim comparisons, found no direct covering result. A graph-incidence interpretation is an elementary consequence of the published transformed equation; whether it was already formulated elsewhere, and whether an older stability calculation can be repurposed to cover the Fourier formula, remain specific historical-priority risks. The distinct complete inverse-and-quantitative claim is judged original on the inspected evidence, provisionally.

value.rationale: An exactly observed edge growth profile is a natural output of the recently established homogenization theorem, so the inverse question of whether it identifies hidden node activity is intrinsic rather than artificially sliced. Graph bipartiteness is shown to be a necessary and sufficient identifiability condition on every finite connected graph, with complete positive fibers. The exact Fourier susceptibility on cycles establishes sharp finite-size amplification and a nontrivial alpha=1/2 large-size crossover; even rings exhibit exact nonidentifiability despite high gain in nearby modes. Together these provide a meaningful structural boundary and quantitative conditioning that qualitative convergence alone does not determine.
